claims.text: Post-deformation annealing controls the formation and retention of short-range chemical order in predominantly FCC high-entropy alloys.
Post-deformation annealing controls the formation and retention of minor phase precipitates in the proposed alloy.
Short-range order and minor precipitates govern the balance between partial-dislocation and twinning mechanisms at the crack tip and thereby determine toughness.
The Cantor alloy CrMnFeCoNi can possess a single-phase FCC structure.
An as-deformed, solution-annealed CrMnFeCoNi starting condition has minimal preexisting short-range order.
The proposed starting condition has minimal second-phase content.
Changing annealing temperature and time can systematically vary short-range order.
Changing annealing temperature and time can systematically vary minor-phase formation.
Heat-treatment-induced changes in short-range order can cause a dramatic change in dislocation-slip behavior.
Short-range order modifies partial-dislocation activity and twinning specifically near a crack tip.
Partial-dislocation and twinning behavior can enhance or limit crack bridging and crack deflection.
Highly ordered or finely precipitated conditions promote dislocation-based toughening.
Disordered or coarsely precipitated conditions reduce crack-tip shielding and lower toughness.
Moderate annealing will produce higher fracture toughness than both under-annealed and over-annealed conditions.
Under-annealed specimens will exhibit negligible short-range order.
Over-annealed specimens will exhibit coarse secondary phases.
The proposed mechanism should primarily apply while the alloy retains an FCC matrix without extensive phase transformation.
After extensive precipitation or transformation, toughness may be controlled more by those transformations than by short-range order.
Direct evidence connecting local chemical order to macroscopic fracture toughness is limited.
Failure to observe toughness or crack-tip-mechanism changes after demonstrably changing short-range order and minor-phase content would falsify the proposed governing role.
